summary: The revision cuts about 3,000 source words to roughly the target while keeping the essential beats: password inference, curtained recess, numbered arrivals, Number One's portrait, locked door and bedroom detour, the council business, the 29th, the honest-men line, Clymes and Fourteen, the document, the girl and the blow. Planned dependencies survive, as do the ambiguity about Mr. Brown and the unnamed attacker. Tommy's inferences mostly stay tentative. Remaining losses are small: the hedge on Number One's nationality, the Russian's deferential refusal of the chair, and the summary of the gathering's variety.

coverage.assessment: The password inference, the 'wrong number' relief, the doorkeeper's limited knowledge, the locked door leading to the bedroom detour, and Boris/money/Ireland all work. Cutting the Potter exchange leaves the Sinn Feiner's 'money is conveyed in easily enough' abrupt but intact, since it stays paired with the Belfast quip. The stated reason for hiding (watch first, then copy a newcomer) is thinner, though the 'Lucky I didn't roll in' line recovers it.

Layout is clear: recess opposite the left-hand door, view of the stairs, shoes left behind the curtain, second door, rusty bolt, portière. The speakers 'the German', 'the Russian' and 'Boris' are tentatively attributed. The one blur is 'The German insisted that he take the head of the table', where 'he' is briefly ambiguous.

Turn-taking in the council is clean, with Number One's questions and the German's answers in order. Fourteen's idiom ('gov'nor', 'I does') and the Russian's sibilance survive. The 'Nothing; but----' / 'But what?' beats are compressed to a direct start but still read as hesitation.

The source's hedge that nothing but the cheekbones indicated the newcomer's nationality is cut, and the narration then calls him 'the Russian' flatly. Elsewhere hedges such as 'rather thought' and 'fancied' are kept.

No premature identification: Mr. Brown's presence stays open ('possible that he is among us now'), no familiar face is named, and the attacker is unseen. The fear reaction of the group is slightly reduced, but 'uneasy faces' and the doubtful glances remain.

Tommy's slow practical voice, the 'dirty trick' indignation and the bulldog line survive. The step-by-step suspense is shortened, which the plan permits. The rhetorical build in the source ('The common criminal... Truly a strange and sinister gathering!') is lost.

The political argument is intact: they use the Labour men because they are honest, 'they are soon disposed of afterwards', the leaders may not strike, and the document and the girl are what is missing. The 'cannot seem to interfere too much' and 'instinct of the populace' lines are dropped, with little interpretive loss.

All six dependencies are intact at the local endpoints. Number One's portrait, both half-familiar faces, the spoken date, the password and doorkeeper, the recess with its view, and Fourteen's identity and assignment are all present. No identity is named.

findings.title: Nationality hedge for Number One removed; 'the Russian' becomes flat narration
findings.claim: The source says the cheekbones 'hinted' at Slavonic ancestry and that 'otherwise there was nothing to indicate his nationality.' The revision keeps 'hinted' but drops the qualifier, then calls him 'The Russian' in narration without any intervening Tommy-inference marker. The earlier 'pale Russian' thought was also cut.
findings.reader_effect: A guess from a single physical cue reads as established fact. The plan says the 'German'/'Russian' labels must remain Tommy's inferences.

evidence.quote: otherwise there was nothing to indicate his nationality
The angle of the cheek-bones hinted at his Slavonic ancestry.
The Russian tapped his cheek.

findings.counterevidence: 'Hinted' remains, and the book as a whole labels him 'the Russian' freely, as the source narration also does.
findings.plan_relation: Plan continuity check ('labels remain Tommy's inferences'); the revision does not fully honour it.
findings.minimal_repair: Restore a short clause in P15: 'hinted at his Slavonic ancestry, though otherwise nothing betrayed his nationality.'

findings.title: Seating exchange compressed; Number One's deferential refusal lost and 'he' blurred
findings.claim: In the source the German indicates his own place, the Russian demurs, and the German insists. The revision gives 'The German insisted that he take the head of the table', so the demurral is gone and 'he' is briefly ambiguous between German and Russian.
findings.reader_effect: A small beat of the newcomer's deference and the group's homage is lost, but the 'Number One' payoff and Fourteen shutting the door survive.

evidence.quote: The Russian demurred, but the other insisted.
The German insisted that he take the head of the table.

findings.counterevidence: The next line, 'It is the only possible place... for--Number One', clarifies who is seated and why.
findings.minimal_repair: If words allow: 'The German offered his own place at the head of the table, and the Russian demurred, but he insisted.'

findings.title: Summary of the gathering's variety and Tommy's reaction cut
findings.claim: The source stacks 'the common criminal, the well-bred Irish gentleman, the pale Russian, and the efficient German master of the ceremonies! Truly a strange and sinister gathering!' before the 'who was this man' question. Both drafts reduce this, so V3 now follows a single arrival.
findings.reader_effect: The Brown-as-hub idea is stated, but the cumulative wonder is thinner and the question comes a little earlier than its build-up.

evidence.quote: Truly a strange and sinister gathering!
Certainly Mr. Brown’s organization was a far-reaching concern.

findings.counterevidence: Later paragraphs show the variety directly (criminal, Sinn Feiner, clerk, worker, gentleman). The source list also names the Russian before he arrives, so cutting it avoids an inconsistency.
findings.plan_relation: Plan says keep the variety, which is satisfied through the arrivals; the narrator's flourish is a defensible cut.
findings.minimal_repair: Optionally add after the Sinn Feiner: 'A strange and sinister gathering.'

dependencies.assessment: The revision keeps Number One's pale, small, gentle, Slavonic-cheekbone, light-eyed description and never names him. ANNETTE's 'So that's who Number 1 is' can still recognise a portrait.

evidence.quote: He was a small man, very pale, with a gentle almost womanish air.
"So that's who Number 1 is," said Tommy with his mouth full of eggs and bacon.

dependencies.assessment: Both the working man and the well-born man are given as vaguely familiar and unnamed. The partner draft still has Tommy picking out two photographs, though its explicit 'two faces were familiar' line was cut there, which is not charged to this revision.

evidence.quote: a working man whose face was vaguely familiar to the young man.
His face, again, was not unknown to the watcher, though he could not put a name to it.
Tommy held one up.

dependencies.assessment: The date is spoken explicitly ('The 29th') and recurs in the German's doubt. Tommy's later lever in ch. 017 matches it.

evidence.quote: “The 29th,” the German answered.
"The 29th," said Tommy thoughtfully, "is less than a fortnight ahead—"

dependencies.assessment: The password inference and the doorkeeper's limited knowledge are both kept, and the doorkeeper is not named here. Partner 017 builds on 'with your own password' (though its own production cut the doorkeeper's quoted words).

evidence.quote: not a request for an individual, but in all probability a password used by the gang.
The doorkeeper clearly did not know all the gang by sight
With your own password, wasn't it?

dependencies.assessment: The recess is at the stairhead, half-concealed by a torn velvet curtain, opposite the meeting-room door and commanding the staircase. It matches MR. BROWN's 'ragged curtain hiding the recess'.

evidence.quote: a small recess immediately on his right, half concealed by a torn velvet curtain, directly opposite the left-handed door and commanding a good view of the staircase.
the ragged curtain hiding the recess

dependencies.assessment: Fourteen is the brutish first arrival (brows, jaw), is addressed by the German as 'Number Fourteen' for both the door and the Clymes assignment, and keeps his relish for blood and jewels. ANNETTE's 'evil-looking Number 14' is recognisable.

evidence.quote: had the low beetling brows and criminal jaw of a type Scotland Yard would have recognized at a glance.
“Clymes must go. He is too far-seeing. Number Fourteen will see to that.”
Conrad entered with the evil-looking Number 14

strengths: Tommy's slow, practical reasoning (password inference, doorkeeper's limits, 'trusting luck too far') survives in a few lines, along with the 'Hun'/'Dutchman' idiom and the 'wrong number' relief.

The numbered-arrival procedure (knock, 'Your number, comrade?', 'Fourteen, gov'nor', 'Correct.') and the rising dread of the pale newcomer, with the venomous-snake image intact, are preserved almost verbatim.
The Mr. Brown ambiguity is preserved: 'We have received a message', the unfinished sentence, 'possible that he is among us now', the neighbours eyed doubtfully. No member is identified as Brown.

The council sequence keeps the Sinn Feiner and Belfast quip as a pair, the Moscow denial, the 29th, and the honest-men line verbatim, with Fourteen's grim relish. The Potter cut leaves no dangling residue.

Voices heard through the portière stay tentative ('rather thought was that of Boris', 'fancied was the commanding man's'). The ending, 'The girl?' / 'She is----' then the unattributed blow, keeps the cliffhanger with no attacker named.
